Scene combo · best of five

Paste up to five versions of a scene (same situation or different ones). Claude collects the best punches, comebacks, reactions and slang lines from all of them and sets them into one scene, adding short linking lines only where needed. Scene-by-scene breakdowns

Each pattern is tagged new (with its library ID) or as a repeat. Scripts 3–5: every new pattern is assigned to an existing character (→ Madhu, Mahesh, Master, Budatha, Venki, Father). The film's own names appear only in the conversations; no new characters were created.

Character & slang analysis

How each character speaks, how the pairs create comedy, and how to make fresh slang. Choose a slang type in the scene writer: 5 Uttarandhra types (U1 keeps the original slang), 4 other regional dialects and 5 comic speaking styles. Each character keeps his personality while his tags are converted.

New formulas added to each character (Scripts 3–5)

Pair dynamics

Slang types: 5 Uttarandhra + 9 others

Reference characters and their slang

Dialect layer: the reference speaks North-Andhra (Uttarandhra) Telugu — ఏటి / ఏటవుదాం / పోద్ది / ఉంటది / ఉండింది — with heavy Tenglish. The Master and Mahesh carry it most. New scenes can keep the dialect but should invent their own pet phrases.

How a new scene is built

  1. Pick 5–8 formulas from at least four different families. Never more than two from one family.
  2. Invent a new situation, setting and conflict. No classroom-exam-heist rerun unless you ask for it.
  3. Build a reaction chain: every line causes the next one's mood.
  4. New punchlines, new similes, new nicknames, new pet phrases. Only the mechanism is borrowed.
  5. Deliver the scene, then the A–F analysis: scene, sources, old vs new, characters and slang, originality, estimated usage split.

Originality guardrails

  • No reference dialogue or punchline is reused, even with words swapped.
  • Signature lines of the reference (its proverb twists, its mission name, its catchphrases) stay with the reference. Learn the move, write a new instance.
  • The usage percentage is an estimate of inspiration versus new writing. It is not a legal or copyright guarantee.

Old to New Dialogue Evolution

A full scan of the library, F01 to F648, in order from Batch 1 to Batch 26. For every formula, the PDF shows the old line and the new line side by side, then a step-by-step Telugu explanation: the move that was kept, how the character, situation and slang changed, how new the wording is, the delivery and timing, the punchline, and where it was reused later. 451 pages · about 10 MB · updated 21 Nov 2026.
